after: lost to a fit of dungeon madness
why: The old line framed a madness-table death as self-harm, which is past the family-friendly bar; it now names the madness as the cause.

trigger: the epitaph on the death screen
before: Died as {name} lived: needing a 5 and rolling whatever that was.
after: Died as {name} lived: needing a high roll and rolling whatever that was.
why: A bare face count as the need was roll-under phrasing; every check rolls high now.

trigger: the epitaph on the death screen
before: Needed a 6 on a d10, three separate times. Managed two.
after: Needed three good d10 rolls to top the wall. Managed two.
why: The climb is roll-high and its winning faces change with the wall, fear of heights and armour, so no single face is right.

trigger: the epitaph on the death screen
before: The wall is still standing. {name} is being scraped off it.
after: The wall is still standing. {name} is not.
why: The scraping image was gore; the deadpan contrast carries the joke on its own.

trigger: the epitaph on the death screen
before: Rolled a 1 on the madness table and won the argument with themselves.
after: Rolled on the madness table. The table won.
why: Winning the argument with themselves read as self-harm; the madness table is now the thing that won.

trigger: the epitaph on the death screen
before: The corridor whispered something. {name} took it entirely on board.
after: Lost their wits on floor {floor}. Everything else followed shortly after.
why: Acting on a whisper implied the hero harmed themselves on instruction; it now states the madness and where it happened.

trigger: the epitaph on the death screen
after: Nothing attacked {name}. Dungeon madness is cheaper than monsters, and much quieter.
why: The old punchline pointed at the hero as the killer; it now names dungeon madness as the cause.

trigger: the epitaph on the death screen
before: Cost of living: 4 hp a day. {name} fell behind on the payments.
after: Cost of living: hp, every day without a ration. {name} fell behind on the payments.
why: An unfed day costs the race's upkeep (1 for a Dwarf, 15 for a Troll, halved by Heft), so a flat 4 hp was wrong for many heroes.

trigger: the epitaph on the death screen
before: 1–5 on a d20 avoids it. {name} rolled the way {name} always rolled.
after: 16–20 on a d20 avoids it. {name} rolled the way {name} always rolled.
why: The trap dodge rolls high: a plain hero avoids it on 16–20, which the death-copy test reads off springTrap.

trigger: a board's title, rule and unit (removed by Phase 84 84-09: BOARD_COPY is trimmed to the four NEW PERSONAL BEST rows — title/unit/unitOne only)
before: Everyone you have rolled and lost, deepest first, with what was said over them. Not ranked against anybody.
why: The graveyard keeps only the newest sixty stones, so everyone was untrue past sixty deaths. Phase 84 (BOARD-20, 84-09) retired GRAVEYARD and the BOARD_COPY.yard entry (and every board's mark/col/unitLabel/rule/tab fields) along with the old Leaderboards panel; this line is no longer printed.

trigger: the Leaderboards panel (BOARDS_PANEL_COPY removed by Phase 84 84-09)
before: Your dead only. The world has not been told.
why: The ME scope also shows with Compete on, when every death has been sent, so the world has been told; the line now says only what the view holds. Phase 84 (BOARD-18..25, 84-09) retired the old Leaderboards panel and its BOARDS_PANEL_COPY bank in favour of the v3 panel's LEADERBOARD_COPY; this line is no longer printed.

trigger: the local standing quip (STANDING_LINES removed by Phase 84 84-09)
before: Somewhere in the middle of the pile. Literally.
why: The band covers every place below tenth, including last, so the middle was not always true. Phase 84 (84-09) retired the old panel's STANDING_LINES bank along with the panel; this line is no longer printed.

trigger: the global standing quip (GLOBAL_STANDING_LINES removed by Phase 84 84-09)
before: Top ten. Strangers are studying your corpse.
why: The same bank served the FRIENDS board, where the people ahead were not strangers. Phase 84 (84-09) retired the old panel's global strip and its GLOBAL_STANDING_LINES bank along with it; this line is no longer printed.

before: You placed {rank} of {total}. Somewhere in the middle of the heap. It is warm there, at least.
after: You placed {rank} of {total}. Somewhere in the heap. It is warm in there, at least.
why: The band covers every place below the top hundred, including last, so the middle was not always true.

before: The dungeon rates that a two.
after: The dungeon rates that two out of ten.
why: A bare 'a two' beside a miss read as the die face, which can contradict the roll shown; it now reads as a score.
